title: security-compliance-review-prep-1on1-jordan
content:
Context:
Quick personal prep notes for 1:1 with Maya (compliance lead) — goal is to align on SOC2/ISO readiness status, vendor risk action items, and auditor questions before the kickoff next week. Keep this loose — will hand off polished agenda to Maya after the call.

Goals for the 1:1:
- Confirm which SOC2 controls we expect auditor to prioritize (CC6: change management, CC7: logical access, CC3: system operations).
- Reconcile evidence owners and locations (Confluence vs GCS buckets).
- Clarify vendor-risk scope: which 3rd parties are in-scope for SOC2 vs ISO review.
- Agree next steps/timeline for evidence collection and evidence freeze for Type II period.

Proposed quick agenda (10–15m):
1) Current high-level status (what's green/yellow/red) — 2m
2) Evidence ownership gaps (who owns what) — 4m
3) Vendor risk exceptions & remediation timeline — 4m
4) Questions for external auditor + next milestones — 3m

Notes / Talking points:
- Overall status: most infra controls mapped, still missing finalized change/docs for release engineering (ticket backlog).
- Evidence locations: canonical source = Confluence page (SOC2 Readiness) but several artifacts still only in GitHub PRs or S3 snapshots. Need canonical copies in gs://redwood-compliance-evidence/2026/soc2 with manifest.
- KMS/HSM: verify key rotation proof + KMS policy docs. Emily said rotation run Feb 20; need export of rotation log and KMS IAM policy (owner: infra-team).
- Access reviews: quarterly IAM review due end of March. We need list of service accounts and owners (SEC-324 tracking).
- Pen-test: vendor report received but remediation status incomplete for two CVEs affecting batch processing service. PRs exist but not merged — ensure auditor sees remediation plan/timeline.
- Change management (CC6): release runbooks exist but need one archived approval per production release in last 6 months. Mapping in Confluence but missing evidence for 2025-11 release.

Vendor risk specific:
- Confirm in-scope vendors: Datadog (monitoring), Postgres managed by CloudDB vendor, payments (Stripe), SSO (Okta), data-storage (S3 via AWS).
- Action: ask Maya if we should include small infra vendor (FastCache Inc) — currently classified low-risk but has production access.
- Request: get latest vendor contracts summary from legal (linked artifact JIRA-LEGAL-77).

Open tickets / things to follow up (quick list):
- SEC-324: compile service account owners list (owner: Aaron) — due 2026-03-10
- SEC-356: evidence upload script to copy artifacts to gs://redwood-compliance-evidence (owner: me) — MVP by 2026-03-05
- INFRA-812: provide KMS rotation logs and policy link (owner: infra) — blocked on infra PR merge
- PEN-45: patch CVE-2025-2244 remediation PR (owner: backend team) — due 2026-03-08

Questions for Maya / auditor prep:
- Auditor preferences: do they want original artifact (GitHub commit) or a PDF snapshot in GCS? (ask now to avoid rework)
- For vendor assessments, do we need SOC2 reports from subvendors or is self-attestation sufficient for low-risk vendors?
- For ISO scope alignment, are we including office physical security (APAC sites) or restricting to cloud infra only?
- Evidence retention windows: confirm minimum retention for logs and backups for both SOC2 and ISO evidencing (we assume 12 months, confirm).

Draft follow-ups (post 1:1):
- Send tidy agenda + current status matrix to Maya and Emily (include links to Confluence + GCS manifest) — target: same day.
- Kick off short-run to gather missing artifacts (assign SEC-324 owners and add to weekly security sync).
- If Maya okays, start vendor evidence requests (email template ready in Confluence).

Quick script / checklist reminder (for me):
- Build manifest CSV: artifact_name, owner, location (gs://...), date, control_mapped (SOC2 control ids) — push to gs://redwood-compliance-evidence/2026/manifest.csv
- Snapshot PRs: create single PDF export for each merged PR referenced as evidence (use `gh pr view --json` + wkpdf).
- IAM list: run `gcloud iam service-accounts list` + correlate to OWNER tag in internal registry.

Tone/notes to self:
- Keep 1:1 focused and short — Maya is busy. Bring clear ask for each item.
- Don't go deep into technical remediation in this call; escalate to follow-ups with infra/product owners.

Action items (concrete, with owners):
- Jordan (me): create evidence upload script + manifest (due 2026-03-05) — PR to INFRA repo, link in Confluence.
- Aaron Kim: compile and verify service-account ownership list + IAM access review pre-read (due 2026-03-10).
- Emily Rivera: gather KMS rotation logs & policy excerpts, drop into GCS (due 2026-03-04).
- Backend lead (TBD): merge remediation PRs for PEN-45 and provide verification steps (due 2026-03-08).
- Legal (contact: Priya Patel): confirm which vendor contracts require auditor disclosure (ask Legal -> JIRA-LEGAL-77).

Risks / blockers to highlight:
- Several artifacts are only in ephemeral PR branches, not in canonical storage — auditor may request originals.
- Small vendor (FastCache Inc) with production creds is not in vendor tracking system — potential scope creep or surprise finding.
- Infra team bandwidth: KMS logs and change approvals need infra time; may be delayed by release calendar.

Next check-in cadence:
- Quick status update after 1:1 (email + Confluence update).
- Weekly security sync (Thu 09:30 PT) to track SEC tickets.

References (to paste into email after call):
- SOC2 readiness confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/SOC2+Readiness
- Evidence bucket: gs://redwood-compliance-evidence/2026/soc2
- Tickets: JIRA-SEC-324, JIRA-SEC-356, PEN-45

Notes to paste in calendar invite (short):
- 15m 1:1 to align on SOC2/ISO readiness, vendor scope, and evidence owners. Will finalize agenda after quick sync.

-- end of scratchpad --
